summary: Hironori Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. A former doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020), Tanaka held a post there and is attested as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Hiroo Kashiwagi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) and taught Waso Harada. He served as professor at Matsusaka University (~1982) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.

Hiroo Sato (born 1953) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1981) and later served at Morioka College (~1984–1993) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) specializes in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and the University of Southern California (PhD, ~1990–1998), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (~2005).

Hiroshi Araki (born 1959), a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, completed degrees including a PhD at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and was professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami works in sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiroshi Deguchi (1928–2015) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He later held an academic post at Hokkaido University from approximately 1959 to 1992.

Hiroshi Kanaseki (1927–2018) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University (~1948–1952) and held an academic post at Tenri University from around 1983 to 2000.

Hiroshi Kanno (born 1952), a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo. He held leadership and editorial roles at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology and posts at Toho Kenkyukai and Soka University.

Hiroshi Kuroda (born 1952) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). Around 1982, he served as an associate professor at both Osaka Gakuin University and Osaka Gakuin College.

Hiroshi Marui (born 1952), an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Musashino University and served as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama (1914–1993) worked in Indology and other fields. In 1987, he was attested as a professor at Osaka University and head of the Ayurveda Research Society.

Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having earned an MA at Hiroshima University. At Hiroshima University, he served as associate professor (attested 2015) and later as professor (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Koyasan University, where he served as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Yamashita (born 1953) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

Hirotaka Kato specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hiroyuki Kato (1836–1916) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), Kaisei School (~1869–1877), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui (1905–1983) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Kyoto University from approximately 1926 to 1929. He later held an academic appointment at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–1978).

Hisao Inagaki (1929–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Ryukoku University and SOAS (PhD, 1968). He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki (1918–1996), a scholar of Buddhist studies, studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1940). He held professorships at Kobe University (~1963–1969) and Komazawa University (~1982–1989), and was professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1982–1996).
